title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (end of §8 header on the previous page). X is a space stratified by a family of closed subspaces (X_i)_{i∈I}, with I partially ordered by i ≤ j iff X_i ⊂ X_j, so minimal elements are the deepest, closed strata. In addition there is a family (B_α, ξ_α)_{α∈Λ}. Each B_α is a 'cylindrical' boundary-type subspace with a germ of cylindrical (collar) neighbourhood ξ_α. The B_α are mutually transverse and transverse to the X_i. This is a stratified space with a system of corner/boundary faces, each equipped with collar germs.

The page defines, by induction on card I, a 'donnée de conicité' (conic structure) on (X, (X_i), (B_α, ξ_α)).

- Base case: if I = ∅ there is exactly one structure, the empty one.
- Inductive step: let I_0 be the set of minimal elements of I and X_{I_0} = ∪_{β∈I_0} X_β, the union of the deepest strata. A conic structure consists of (a) and (b) below.

(a) A strict conic neighbourhood T_{I_0} of X_{I_0}. It is transverse to the (B_α, ξ_α), and hence transverse to all the X_i. By §7 (structure (19)), such a tube lets one cut X open. One deletes the open tube and gets X*, a space with new boundary pieces. The data are:
- (22): X*; its induced stratification (X_i*)_{i∈I*} with I* = I \ I_0; and the enlarged transverse family of cylindrical boundary pieces. That family consists of the old faces B_α restricted to X*, with their collars ξ_α, and the new faces Ẋ_β (the boundary sphere-bundles or links of the tube over X_β, β∈I_0), with collars ξ_β given by the conic/radial structure.
- (23): the deleted strata X_β (β∈I_0) themselves, with the induced boundary/collar data (B_{βα}, ξ_{βα}).

(b) A conic structure on (22). This makes sense by induction because card I* < card I.

Unwinding the recursion gives a sequence of tube-removals, deepest strata first. It ends with a manifold-with-corners-like 'déploiement' (unfolding) of X. Each corner face carries cylindrical germs, and the faces are fibred over lower strata via the tube projections.

Purpose: an intrinsic, tube-based combinatorial definition of a conelike (Thom–Mather type) structure, adapted to the 'déploiement' viewpoint of the title. The next page goes on to:
- conjecture existence of such structures under non-degeneracy hypotheses (and equisingular versions);
- ask whether the notion is independent of the chosen filtration of I by successive layers of minimal elements;
- propose replacing the family (B_α) by a cylindrical stratification of type |S(Λ)|.
errors: No mathematical error is visible; this is a definition. Gap: the assertion that transversality to the (B_α, ξ_α) 'conséquemment' gives transversality to all X_i depends on the transversality hypotheses fixed earlier and is not justified here.

Gap: 'strict conic neighbourhood' and the construction of the collars ξ_β on the new faces Ẋ_β are taken from §7 / formula (19). The page does not check that the new family remains mutually transverse, which the recursion in (b) needs.
The annotation 'stratification de I*' should be read as 'stratification of X* indexed by I*'.

ideas.what: Inductive definition of a conic structure: remove a strict conic tube around the minimal (deepest) strata, then demand a conic structure on the resulting stratified space with boundary, by induction on the number of strata.
ideas.modern_name: Control data / systems of tubular neighbourhoods (Thom–Mather); inductive 'unzipping' or resolution of conically stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom (1969), Mather (1970) for control data; Verona (1984) for resolution; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017) for unzipping of conically smooth spaces
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme of a theory of 'déploiements' of stratified spaces appears, in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6; this definition does not.

ideas.what: Bookkeeping of boundary faces: each step adds the link-bundle boundaries Ẋ_β, with their radial collars, to the existing transverse family of cylindrical faces (B_α, ξ_α). This produces manifold-with-corners-type data.
ideas.modern_name: Manifolds with fibred corners / resolution of stratified spaces (iterated edge structures)

ideas.what: Choosing the layer I_0 of minimal elements; the whole recursion depends on this filtration of the poset I.
ideas.modern_name: Depth filtration of a stratified space

missed.claim: This is an explicit 1981–82 inductive definition of a conic/unfolding structure. It tracks the transverse cylindrical boundary faces created at each tube-removal, which is essentially the resolution of a stratified space into a manifold with fibred corners. It is not credited to Grothendieck in the literature, which attributes such constructions to Verona, Melrose's school and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka.
missed.quote: famille transversale de sous-espaces bords "cylindriques" de X différents des X_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows that Grothendieck's 'déploiement' programme from the Esquisse had a concrete technical form matching later resolution / unzipping theory. That is of historical interest, and possibly a source for a tame-topology version of it.

missed.claim: The recursion is set up, but neither existence of such structures nor their uniqueness up to isotopy is proved here. The following page leaves both, and independence from the filtration, as questions.
missed.quote: Une structure conique sur (22) (ce qui a un sens, par récurrence...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Independence from the order of unzipping, and the contractibility of the space of such structures, are statements of current interest in conically smooth / tame stratified homotopy theory.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean unpublished definition that anticipates resolution and unzipping of stratified spaces. However, the underlying ideas (control data, inductive tube removal) were standard since Thom–Mather, and the page is a definition rather than a result.
transcription_corrections: In (22) the symbol read as 'ξB_α' looks like a struck-over symbol before B_α. It is probably the restriction of B_α to X* (or ∂B_α), not ξ·B_α.
The note under X_i* reads 'stratification de I*' in the image. It means the stratification of X* indexed by I*.

In (a), the struck word before 'aux (B_α, ξ_α)' and the inserted 'voisinage conique strict' above the struck word are rendered correctly in sense. The phrase 'transversal aux (B_α, ξ_α)' appears in the image (partly struck and rewritten).
